newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares rise but foreign backing weak.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares rise but foreign backing weak.

text.p: Russian investors cheered by Thursday's market gains, the first uptick in a week, have rushed on to the market and are pushing up prices of leading shares, traders said on Friday.
But operators said the morning firmness did not indicate the market had begun a bull run and added many Western investors who generally determine tone were still on the sidelines.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 463.28 after 462.37 at Thursday's close.
Local utility Irkutskenergo IRGZ.RTS jumped to $0.339 at 0950 GMT from $0.330 and Rostelekom RTKM.RTS long distance telecoms company had risen to $4.58 from $4.37.

United City Bank senior trader Samit Yakovlev said most leading shares were in demand, following Rostelekom which was rising on expectations that an annual meeting by mail, requiring postmarks no later than Friday, would produce good news.
Shareholders are voting on a capital increase and new board, following the transfer of the government's 38 percent stake to telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, itself being sold off.
"Some stability has arrived," he said. "Prices are low enough, so that it is time to buy."

But Aton trader Boris Shvedsky said the upward move, which broke a week's downward consolidation from a sharp 30 percent rise beginning in mid-June, appeared temporary and that most buyers were local, especially banks.
"Western demand is still moderate," he said.
Westerners and Russians had been seen buying on Thursday, cheered by strong U.S. and emerging markets performances. The Dow Jones slipped on profit-taking on Thursday.
Yakovlev said many investors in Russia were waiting for August, expecting lower prices on a summer slump.
